definition: The fresh grass that springs up after a meadow has been mown; aftermath. In some dialects, it can also mean the remaining stubble in a harvested field.
etymology: It comes from Old English edisc, meaning an enclosed pasture or park. Over time, the word settled on the particular pasture-growth that returns after the hay has gone—a small green encore at summer’s end.
usage: By September’s close, the meadow had put out a tender eddish, bright against the cut hay.
